source_row.item_data_json: {"options":{"A":"Attempting to physically restrain the client's arms and legs in an effort to stop the ongoing seizure activity from continuing any further","B":"Placing a padded object directly into the client's mouth in an effort to prevent them from accidentally biting down on their own tongue","C":"Protecting the client from injury, turning them to the side if possible, and timing the seizure, without restraining movements or placing anything in the mouth","D":"Restraining the client's movements entirely in an effort to bring the ongoing seizure activity to a quicker end sooner than it would naturally"}}
source_row.rationale: Appropriate seizure first aid includes protecting the client from injury (such as clearing the area of hazards), turning them to the side if possible (to help maintain airway patency), and timing the seizure duration, while avoiding restraining movements or placing anything in the mouth, both of which can cause injury.
source_row.source_name: Epilepsy Foundation — Seizure First Aid Guidelines
